questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In Werner's study of cobalt(III) ammine chlorides, two compounds of the same empirical formula CoCl₃·4NH₃ were obtained, one green and one violet. Both are formulated as [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl. The two compounds are:

solution.concept: Werner's cobalt ammine complexes and geometrical isomerism
solution.explanation: Both compounds contain the same complex cation [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ and the same counter ion, so they are not structural isomers. They differ only in the arrangement of the two Cl⁻ ligands around cobalt: next to each other (cis) or opposite each other (trans). Such compounds are geometrical isomers.
steps: Same formula and same ions in and out of the coordination sphere → not ionisation/coordination isomers
No ambidentate ligand → not linkage isomers
Octahedral [MA₄B₂] → cis and trans forms → geometrical isomers
solution.why_others_wrong: Ionisation isomers exchange a ligand with a counter ion; linkage isomers need an ambidentate ligand; coordination isomers need both a complex cation and a complex anion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory (Table of CoCl₃·nNH₃ compounds) and isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option B: Geometrical (cis and trans) isomers

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Impure nickel is purified by converting it into nickel tetracarbonyl, which is later decomposed:
Ni + 4CO → [Ni(CO)₄]
The volume of carbon monoxide, measured at STP, needed to convert 5.9 g of nickel completely into [Ni(CO)₄] is (Ni = 59; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the formation of a metal carbonyl used in metal purification
solution.explanation: One mole of nickel combines with four moles of CO. The volatile carbonyl is separated and decomposed to give pure nickel.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.24 L takes Ni : CO as 1 : 1 and 4.48 L as 1 : 2. 17.92 L doubles the correct amount.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications (purification of nickel)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the extraction of gold, the metal combines with cyanide in the presence of oxygen and water to form the soluble complex [Au(CN)₂]⁻. Gold is then recovered in the metallic form from this solution by adding:

solution.concept: Complex formation in the extraction of metals
solution.explanation: Gold forms the coordination entity [Au(CN)₂]⁻ in aqueous solution. Zinc, a more reactive metal, displaces gold from this complex, and gold separates as the metal.
steps: Zinc added → gold separates in metallic form
solution.why_others_wrong: Silver nitrate and ammonia do not reduce the complex to gold; dimethylglyoxime is the reagent for estimating Ni²⁺.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications (extraction of metals)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Crystal field theory does not take into account the covalent character of the bonding between the ligand and the central atom.
Statement II: As crystal field theory treats ligands as point charges, anionic ligands such as I⁻, Br⁻ and Cl⁻ are actually found at the strong-field end of the spectrochemical series.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Limitations of crystal field theory
solution.explanation: CFT treats the metal–ligand bond as purely ionic, so it ignores covalent character (Statement I is true). If ligands were simple point charges, anions should cause the largest splitting; in fact the halide ions lie at the weak-field (low) end of the spectrochemical series. This contradiction is listed in NCERT as a limitation of CFT, so Statement II is false.
steps: Statement I: a stated limitation of CFT → true
Statement II: halide ions are at the low (weak-field) end → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', limitations of crystal field theory
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: cis-Platin, cis-[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], is used to inhibit the growth of tumours. The percentage of platinum by mass in cis-platin is (Pt = 195, N = 14, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Percentage composition of a coordination compound
solution.explanation: Molar mass of [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] = 195 + 2(17) + 2(35.5) = 300 g mol⁻¹. Platinum makes up 195 g of this.
solution.why_others_wrong: 73.3% leaves out the two NH₃ ligands; 85.2% leaves out the two Cl ligands; 32.5% halves the correct value.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications (cis-platin)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of K[Cr(H₂O)₂(C₂O₄)₂]·3H₂O is:

solution.concept: Naming an anionic coordination entity
solution.explanation: The complex ion is an anion, so the metal name ends in -ate (chromate). Ligands are listed alphabetically: aqua before oxalato. Oxidation state: x + 2(0) + 2(−2) = −1, so x = +3. The water of crystallisation is named last as 'trihydrate'.
steps: Anionic complex → chromate; ligands alphabetical: diaqua, dioxalato
solution.why_others_wrong: 'chromium' is used only when the complex is a cation or neutral; oxalato before aqua breaks the alphabetical order; chromium is +3, not +2.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature of coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In photography, unexposed silver bromide is dissolved by hypo:
AgBr + 2Na₂S₂O₃ → Na₃[Ag(S₂O₃)₂] + NaBr
The minimum mass of hypo crystals, Na₂S₂O₃·5H₂O (molar mass 248 g mol⁻¹), needed to dissolve 0.94 g of AgBr is (Ag = 108, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of complex formation with thiosulphate
solution.explanation: Each AgBr needs two thiosulphate ions to form the soluble complex [Ag(S₂O₃)₂]³⁻.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.24 g takes a 1 : 1 ratio; 1.58 g uses the anhydrous molar mass (158); 4.96 g doubles the thiosulphate again.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications (photography)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ruby is red whereas emerald is green, although in both gemstones the colour is due to Cr³⁺ ions occupying octahedral sites.
Reason (R): The crystal field splitting experienced by Cr³⁺ is different in aluminium oxide (ruby) and in the mineral beryl (emerald), so light of different wavelengths is absorbed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Colour of gemstones from crystal field splitting
solution.explanation: In ruby, Cr³⁺ ions replace some Al³⁺ ions in Al₂O₃; in emerald, Cr³⁺ ions occupy octahedral sites in beryl, Be₃Al₂Si₆O₁₈. The different surroundings change the magnitude of the splitting, so the absorption bands of emerald are shifted and it transmits green light. R gives exactly this reason for A.
steps: Different host lattice → different Δo → different light absorbed
R explains the difference in colour stated in A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', colour in coordination compounds (ruby and emerald)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Carnallite, KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O, dissociates completely into simple ions when dissolved in water.
(b) An aqueous solution of K₄[Fe(CN)₆] does not contain Fe²⁺ ions released from the complex ion, because [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ does not dissociate into Fe²⁺ and CN⁻.
(c) In [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂], the coordination number of platinum is 2.
(d) In [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl, the primary valence of cobalt is 3 and its secondary valence is 6.
(e) Potash alum keeps its identity as a complex ion when dissolved in water.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Double salts versus coordination compounds; Werner's valences
solution.explanation: Double salts such as carnallite, Mohr's salt and potash alum dissociate completely into simple ions in water, whereas a complex ion such as [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ stays intact. In [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] four donor atoms (2 N, 2 Cl) are bonded to Pt, so its coordination number is 4. In [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl the primary valence (oxidation state) is 3 and the secondary valence (coordination number) is 6.
steps: (b) complex ion does not dissociate → true
(e) potash alum is a double salt → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (e), which are false, or leaves out (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory; double salts and complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The complex ion [Co(C₂O₄)₃]³⁻ is found to be diamagnetic (Z of Co = 27). According to valence bond theory, the hybridisation of cobalt and the shape of the complex are:

solution.concept: Using magnetic data to decide the hybridisation (VBT)
solution.explanation: Cobalt is +3 (3 × −2 = −6, overall −3), so it is d⁶. Being diamagnetic, all six d electrons are paired in three 3d orbitals, leaving two inner 3d orbitals free. These, with 4s and three 4p orbitals, give d²sp³ hybridisation: an inner orbital, octahedral complex.
steps: Diamagnetic → electrons paired in three 3d orbitals
solution.why_others_wrong: sp³d² would leave four unpaired electrons (paramagnetic). Three didentate oxalate ions give coordination number 6, so square planar and tetrahedral shapes are impossible.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', bonding: valence bond theory

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The IUPAC name of [Co(NH₃)₄Cl(NO₂)]Cl is tetraamminechloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III) chloride.
Statement II: The IUPAC name of K₂[PtCl₆] is potassium hexachloridoplatinum(IV).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Naming cationic and anionic complexes
solution.explanation: Statement I: ligands in alphabetical order (ammine, chlorido, nitrito-N); Co: x + 0 − 1 − 1 = +1, so x = +3. The name is correct. Statement II: [PtCl₆]²⁻ is an anion, so the metal must be named platinate: potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV).
steps: I: alphabetical order and oxidation state +3 are correct → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature of coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ni²⁺ is estimated gravimetrically with dimethylglyoxime (DMG). The nickel in 0.50 g of an alloy is converted completely into the red precipitate Ni(DMG)₂ (molar mass 289 g mol⁻¹, one Ni per formula unit), which weighs 0.578 g after drying. The percentage of nickel in the alloy is (Ni = 59):

solution.concept: Gravimetric estimation of nickel with a chelating ligand
solution.explanation: Each mole of Ni(DMG)₂ contains one mole of Ni, so the mass of Ni is found from the moles of precipitate and then compared with the mass of the alloy.
solution.why_others_wrong: 20.4% is the percentage of Ni in the precipitate, not in the alloy. 47.2% counts two Ni per formula unit. 11.8% divides by 1.0 g instead of 0.50 g.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications (estimation of Ni²⁺ with DMG)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct? (Atomic numbers: Ti 22, V 23, Cr 24, Mn 25, Co 27)

(a) [Cr(CN)₆]³⁻ is an inner orbital (d²sp³) complex with three unpaired electrons.
(b) [Mn(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is a low-spin complex with one unpaired electron.
(c) [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic.
(d) [V(H₂O)₆]³⁺ has two unpaired electrons.
(e) [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Unpaired electrons and hybridisation from d-electron counts
solution.explanation: Cr³⁺ is d³: whatever the ligand, three unpaired electrons in t₂g, and two empty 3d orbitals allow d²sp³. Mn²⁺ is d⁵; with strong-field CN⁻ the electrons pair to t₂g⁵, leaving one unpaired. Ti³⁺ is d¹ (paramagnetic). V³⁺ is d² (two unpaired). Co³⁺ with CN⁻ is low-spin t₂g⁶ (diamagnetic).
steps: Mn²⁺ d⁵ low spin → t₂g⁵ → 1 unpaired → (b) true
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (c) or (e), both false, or leave out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory and magnetic properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following compounds gives a white precipitate immediately with aqueous AgNO₃ AND can also exist as geometrical isomers? (All are octahedral cobalt(III) compounds.)

solution.concept: Ionisable chloride and geometrical isomerism together
solution.explanation: A precipitate with AgNO₃ needs Cl⁻ outside the coordination sphere. Geometrical isomerism in an octahedral complex needs a pattern such as [MA₄B₂] or [MA₃B₃]. [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]Cl has one ionisable Cl⁻ and a cation [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ that exists as cis and trans forms.
steps: [Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃]: fac/mer isomers but no ionisable Cl⁻ → no precipitate
[Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ and [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃: precipitate, but [MA₅B] and [MA₆] have no geometrical isomers
solution.why_others_wrong: Each other compound meets only one of the two conditions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory and geometrical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the complex ion in List-I with the stereoisomerism it shows in List-II (en = ethane-1,2-diamine; all are octahedral).

List-I:
A. [Co(en)₃]³⁺
B. [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺
C. [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺
D. [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺

List-II:
I. Both geometrical and optical isomerism
II. Optical isomerism only
III. Geometrical isomerism only
IV. Neither geometrical nor optical isomerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Recognising geometrical and optical isomerism in octahedral complexes
solution.explanation: [Co(en)₃]³⁺ has only one arrangement of three chelate rings but exists as non-superimposable mirror images (optical only). [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ has cis and trans forms, both with a mirror plane (geometrical only). [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ has cis and trans forms, and the cis form is chiral (both). [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺ has only one form.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap optical-only with geometrical-only, or give [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]²⁺ an isomer it cannot have.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', stereoisomerism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The crystal field splitting energy Δo of [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ is greater than that of [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺.
Reason (R): For the same ligand, the magnitude of Δo increases as the charge on the central metal ion increases.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Dependence of Δo on the charge of the metal ion
solution.explanation: NCERT states that Δo depends on the field produced by the ligand and on the charge of the metal ion. With the same ligand (H₂O) and the same metal, Fe³⁺ (higher charge, smaller ion) draws the ligands closer and causes a larger splitting than Fe²⁺. R is the reason for A.
steps: Same ligand and metal; only the charge differs
Higher charge → stronger interaction → larger Δo
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory (factors affecting Δo)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: On complete combustion, 0.25 g of an organic compound gives 0.135 g of water. The percentage of hydrogen in the compound is (H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Estimation of hydrogen (Liebig's method)
solution.explanation: All the hydrogen of the compound ends up in the water. 18 g of water contains 2 g of hydrogen.
solution.why_others_wrong: 54.0% is the mass of water as a percentage of the sample. 3.0% uses 1/18 instead of 2/18. 12.0% uses 4/18.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of carbon and hydrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In paper chromatography, the strip of paper on which the components of a mixture have been separated, after the solvent has risen through it, is known as a(n):

solution.concept: Terms used in paper chromatography
solution.explanation: A strip of special paper, with a spot of the mixture near the bottom, is placed in a solvent. As the solvent rises, the components travel to different heights. The developed paper strip is called a chromatogram.
solution.why_others_wrong: The eluant is the solvent (mobile phase) that runs through the column or paper; an adsorbent is used in adsorption chromatography; 'stationary front' is not a chromatography term.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', partition chromatography

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In the estimation of phosphorus, 0.20 g of an organic compound is oxidised, and the phosphoric acid formed is precipitated as ammonium phosphomolybdate, (NH₄)₃PO₄·12MoO₃ (molar mass 1877 g mol⁻¹). The dry precipitate weighs 1.877 g. The percentage of phosphorus in the compound is (P = 31):

solution.concept: Estimation of phosphorus as ammonium phosphomolybdate
solution.explanation: One formula unit of ammonium phosphomolybdate contains one phosphorus atom.
solution.why_others_wrong: 31.0% counts two P per formula unit; 7.8% halves the answer; 3.1% divides by 1 g instead of 0.20 g.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of phosphorus

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In the estimation of carbon and hydrogen, 0.46 g of ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is burnt completely in a stream of oxygen. The products are passed first through a U-tube of anhydrous CaCl₂ and then through a bulb of concentrated KOH solution. The increases in mass of the CaCl₂ tube and of the KOH bulb are, respectively (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Absorbents used in Liebig's combustion method
solution.explanation: Anhydrous CaCl₂ absorbs the water and concentrated KOH absorbs the carbon dioxide. One mole of C₂H₆O gives 2 mol CO₂ and 3 mol H₂O.
steps: H₂O = 0.03 mol = 0.54 g (gain of CaCl₂ tube)
CO₂ = 0.02 mol = 0.88 g (gain of KOH bulb)
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.88 g and 0.54 g swaps the absorbents. 0.27 g and 0.44 g halves both amounts. 0.54 g and 0.44 g counts only one CO₂ per molecule.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of carbon and hydrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If a compound is highly soluble in one solvent and only slightly soluble in another, its crystallisation can be carried out satisfactorily in a mixture of the two solvents.
Statement II: The Prussian blue colour obtained in the Lassaigne's test for nitrogen is due to the formation of iron(III) thiocyanate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Crystallisation from mixed solvents; chemistry of the test for nitrogen
solution.explanation: NCERT notes that crystallisation can be done in a mixture of two solvents in such a case (Statement I true). The Prussian blue is iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃·xH₂O, formed from the sodium cyanide of the fusion extract; iron(III) thiocyanate gives the blood-red colour seen when both N and S are present (Statement II false).
steps: II: Prussian blue = Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃·xH₂O, not a thiocyanate → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', crystallisation; detection of nitrogen
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur is fused with an excess of sodium, the extract gives the Prussian blue test for nitrogen and the sodium nitroprusside test for sulphur.
Reason (R): With excess sodium, the sodium thiocyanate first formed decomposes into sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Lassaigne's test when nitrogen and sulphur are both present
solution.explanation: With a limited amount of sodium, N and S together form NaSCN, which gives a blood-red colour with Fe³⁺ but no Prussian blue (no free CN⁻). With excess sodium, NaSCN breaks down to NaCN and Na₂S, and these ions then give their usual tests. R is exactly the reason for A.
steps: Limited Na → NaSCN (blood red with Fe³⁺)
CN⁻ → Prussian blue; S²⁻ → violet with nitroprusside; R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', Lassaigne's test
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: 0.59 g of an organic compound containing one nitrogen atom per molecule is analysed by Kjeldahl's method. The ammonia evolved exactly neutralises 10.0 mL of 0.50 M H₂SO₄. The molar mass of the compound is:

solution.concept: Kjeldahl's method used to find a molar mass
solution.explanation: H₂SO₄ is dibasic, so one mole of it neutralises two moles of NH₃. Each molecule of the compound gives one NH₃.
solution.why_others_wrong: 118 g mol⁻¹ forgets that H₂SO₄ is dibasic. 29.5 g mol⁻¹ multiplies by 2 once more. 5.9 g mol⁻¹ uses 10.0 mL as 0.10 L.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', Kjeldahl's method

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: Cyclic compounds that contain an atom other than carbon in the ring may be alicyclic or aromatic. Which of the following is an alicyclic heterocyclic compound?

solution.concept: Classification of cyclic organic compounds
solution.explanation: Tetrahydrofuran has an oxygen atom in a saturated five-membered ring, so it is heterocyclic but not aromatic (alicyclic). Pyridine and furan are heterocyclic aromatic compounds; cyclohexane is alicyclic but homocyclic (only carbon in the ring).
steps: Heteroatom in ring + no aromatic π system → tetrahydrofuran
solution.why_others_wrong: Pyridine and furan are aromatic heterocycles; cyclohexane contains no heteroatom.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', classification of organic compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CO–CH₂–CH₂–COOH is:

solution.concept: Naming a compound with a carboxyl and a keto group
solution.explanation: The –COOH group has higher priority than the ketone, so it is the suffix and its carbon is C-1. The ketonic oxygen on C-4 is cited with the prefix 'oxo'.
solution.why_others_wrong: The carboxyl carbon must be C-1; 'keto' is not the IUPAC prefix; the parent is named after the principal group, not as a substituted ketone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of polyfunctional compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The molecular formula of the alkane 3-ethyl-2-methylhexane is:

solution.concept: Working back from an IUPAC name to the molecular formula
solution.explanation: The parent chain has six carbons; an ethyl group adds two and a methyl group one, so there are nine carbon atoms. An open-chain alkane has the formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: C₈H₁₈ counts the ethyl group as one carbon; C₁₀H₂₂ adds a carbon; C₉H₁₈ is the formula of an alkene or cycloalkane, not an alkane.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A σ bond is formed by head-on overlap of orbitals, whereas a π bond is formed by sideways (lateral) overlap of p orbitals.
Statement II: Between the same two carbon atoms, a π bond is stronger than a σ bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: σ and π bonds
solution.explanation: Head-on overlap along the internuclear axis gives a σ bond; parallel p orbitals overlap sideways to give a π bond. Sideways overlap is smaller, so the π bond is weaker than the σ bond; this is why multiple bonds are sites of reaction.
steps: II: π bond is weaker (smaller overlap) → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', shapes of carbon compounds
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the compound in List-I with its class in List-II.

List-I:
A. Butane
B. Cyclohexane
C. Naphthalene
D. Thiophene

List-II:
I. Benzenoid aromatic compound
II. Heterocyclic aromatic compound
III. Open-chain (acyclic) compound
IV. Alicyclic homocyclic compound

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Classification of organic compounds by structure
solution.explanation: Butane has an open chain. Cyclohexane has a ring of carbon atoms only and is not aromatic. Naphthalene contains fused benzene rings (benzenoid). Thiophene has a sulphur atom in an aromatic five-membered ring.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap open-chain with alicyclic, or benzenoid with heterocyclic aromatic.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', classification of organic compounds
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Multiple bonds in organic molecules provide sites for chemical reactions.
Reason (R): The electron cloud of a π bond lies above and below the plane of the bonding atoms, so its electrons are easily available to attacking reagents.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Reactivity of π bonds
solution.explanation: NCERT explains that the π electrons are more exposed than σ electrons because the π cloud lies above and below the bond axis. Attacking reagents (especially electrophiles) can reach them easily, which is why multiple bonds are reactive sites. R explains A.
steps: π electrons exposed above and below the plane
Easily attacked → multiple bond is a reaction site
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', shapes of carbon compounds (π bond)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many esters (structural isomers only) have the molecular formula C₄H₈O₂?

solution.concept: Metamerism among esters
solution.explanation: An ester RCOOR′ with four carbons in all can be built by sharing the carbons between the acyl part and the alkoxy part in different ways; these esters are metamers of one another.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 misses the branched methanoate; 2 counts only the ethanoate and propanoate; 6 includes the two C₄H₈O₂ carboxylic acids, which are not esters.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of OHC–CH₂–CH₂–CH(OH)–CH₃ is:

solution.concept: Principal functional group and numbering
solution.explanation: The aldehyde group outranks the hydroxyl group, so the suffix is '-al' and the CHO carbon is C-1. The –OH group on C-4 is shown by the prefix 'hydroxy'. For an aldehyde, the locant 1 is not written.
solution.why_others_wrong: Numbering must give the aldehyde carbon locant 1; '-one' is a ketone suffix; the alcohol cannot be the suffix when an aldehyde is present.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of polyfunctional compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When the inductive and electromeric effects operate in opposite directions, the electromeric effect predominates.
Statement II: The –OCOR group attached to a benzene ring through its oxygen atom shows a +R (electron-releasing) effect.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Electromeric effect versus inductive effect; +R groups
solution.explanation: NCERT states that the electromeric effect predominates when the two act in opposite directions. It also lists –OCOR among the groups that show a +R effect (along with halogen, –OH, –OR, –NH₂, –NHR, –NR₂ and –NHCOR), because the oxygen lone pair attached to the ring can be delocalised into it.
steps: II: lone pair on O bonded to the ring → +R → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', electromeric and resonance effects
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

A. (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃
B. CH₃CH₂–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₃

I. 3-Methylpent-2-ene
II. 2,2-Dimethylpropan-1-ol
III. 2-Methylpentane

solution.concept: Applying IUPAC rules to branched compounds
solution.explanation: A: five-carbon chain with a methyl on C-2 → 2-methylpentane. B: the longest chain has five carbons; choosing the chain with more substituents gives ethyl on C-3 and methyl on C-2 → 3-ethyl-2-methylpentane. C: the double bond gets the lower locant (C-2) and the methyl is on C-3 → 3-methylpent-2-ene. D: three-carbon chain with –OH on C-1 and two methyls on C-2 → 2,2-dimethylpropan-1-ol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about resonance (canonical) structures are correct?

(a) Among canonical structures, the one with more covalent bonds is more stable.
(b) A canonical structure in which all atoms (other than hydrogen) have complete octets is more stable than one in which some atom lacks an octet.
(c) The molecule keeps changing (flipping) from one canonical structure to another.
(d) A canonical structure with the positive charge on the more electronegative atom contributes more to the hybrid.
(e) The difference in energy between the actual structure and the lowest-energy resonance structure is called the resonance stabilisation energy.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Rules for the stability of canonical structures
solution.explanation: A structure is more stable when it has more covalent bonds, complete octets, less separation of opposite charges, a negative charge on the more electronegative atom and a positive charge on the more electropositive atom. The canonical forms are hypothetical; the molecule is a single hybrid and does not flip between them. The energy lowering relative to the most stable canonical form is the resonance energy.
steps: (d) positive charge should be on the more electropositive atom → false
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (c) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the curved-arrow notation, the homolytic cleavage of a covalent bond is shown with full-headed curved arrows.
Reason (R): In homolytic cleavage, each of the two bonded atoms keeps one electron of the shared pair.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Curved arrows for homolytic and heterolytic cleavage
solution.explanation: A full-headed arrow shows the movement of an electron pair (heterolysis). In homolysis each atom takes one electron, and the movement of a single electron is shown by a half-headed (fish-hook) arrow. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: homolysis uses fish-hook (half-headed) arrows → false
R: one electron to each atom → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', fission of a covalent bond
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

options.text: lies in the plane of the paper
projects out of the plane of the paper towards the observer
projects out of the plane of the paper away from the observer

solution.concept: Wedge-and-dash formulas
solution.explanation: Bonds in the plane of the paper are drawn as normal lines, a solid wedge shows a bond pointing out of the paper towards the viewer, and a dashed wedge a bond pointing away from the viewer.
steps: Dashed wedge → away from the observer

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: In which of the following molecules are sp³, sp² and sp hybridised carbon atoms all present?

solution.concept: Identifying hybridisation from the bonding of each carbon
solution.explanation: A carbon with four single bonds is sp³, one with a double bond is sp², and one with a triple bond is sp. In CH₃–CH=CH–C≡N the carbons are sp³, sp², sp² and sp.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each other molecule lacks one of the three hybridisation states.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hybridisation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The total number of stereoisomers (geometrical and optical together) of pent-3-en-2-ol, CH₃–CH=CH–CH(OH)–CH₃, is:

solution.concept: Combining geometrical and optical isomerism
solution.explanation: The C=C bond carries different groups on each carbon (H and CH₃; H and CH(OH)CH₃), so cis and trans forms exist. C-2 is bonded to H, OH, CH₃ and CH=CHCH₃, four different groups, so it is chiral. The two features are independent, giving 2 × 2 stereoisomers.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 counts only one kind of isomerism; 3 is the answer for a molecule with two identical chiral centres (meso form); 8 assumes three stereogenic units.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
In which of the following conversions is the change in hybridisation of the indicated carbon atom(s) described correctly?

(a) CH₂=CH₂ + Br₂ → BrCH₂–CH₂Br: each carbon changes from sp² to sp³.
(b) HC≡CH + H₂ (Lindlar catalyst) → CH₂=CH₂: each carbon changes from sp to sp².
(c) C₆H₆ + Cl₂ (anhydrous FeCl₃) → C₆H₅Cl: the ring carbon bonded to chlorine in the product is sp³.
(d) CH₃CH₂OH (conc. H₂SO₄, 443 K) → CH₂=CH₂: both carbons change from sp³ to sp².
(e) CH₃COOH + SOCl₂ → CH₃COCl: the carbonyl carbon changes from sp² to sp³.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Hybridisation changes in addition, elimination and substitution
solution.explanation: Addition to a multiple bond raises the number of σ bonds on the carbons (sp² → sp³, sp → sp²). Elimination does the reverse (sp³ → sp²). In substitution reactions the hybridisation of the reacting carbon is the same in the reactant and the product: the aromatic carbon in chlorobenzene and the acyl carbon in CH₃COCl remain sp².
steps: (e) acyl chloride carbon is sp²: false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option includes (c) or (e), both false, or leaves out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hybridisation and types of organic reactions

Statement I: CH₃–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃ is named 3-methylpentane.
Statement II: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH₃ is named 3-ethyl-2-methylbutane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Choosing the longest chain that runs through a substituent
solution.explanation: Statement I: the longest chain runs through the ethyl group and has five carbons with a methyl on C-3, so the name 3-methylpentane is correct. Statement II: the longest chain also runs through the ethyl group and has five carbons, with methyl groups on C-2 and C-3; the correct name is 2,3-dimethylpentane.
steps: I: longest chain = 5 C, methyl on C-3 → true
II: longest chain = 5 C → 2,3-dimethylpentane, not a butane → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', IUPAC nomenclature

Match the compound in List-I with the number of sp³-hybridised carbon atoms in it (List-II).

solution.concept: Polyfunctional nomenclature: suffix, numbering and alphabetical prefixes
solution.explanation: –COOH is the principal group, so its carbon is C-1 and the parent is hexanoic acid. The keto oxygen is on C-3 (oxo) and the –OH on C-5 (hydroxy). Prefixes are written in alphabetical order: hydroxy before oxo.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cyclohexane and hex-1-ene are structural isomers.
Reason (R): A cyclic compound and an open-chain compound can never have the same molecular formula.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Isomerism between ring compounds and alkenes
solution.explanation: Both cyclohexane and hex-1-ene have the formula C₆H₁₂; they differ in the way the atoms are joined, so they are structural isomers. Each ring 'uses up' two hydrogens just as a double bond does, so ring compounds and open-chain alkenes often share a formula. R is false.
steps: Cyclohexane: C₆H₁₂; hex-1-ene: C₆H₁₂ → same formula, different structure → A true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism

questions.question_text: In the sawhorse projection of ethane, the central carbon–carbon bond is drawn as a somewhat longer, slightly tilted straight line. The front carbon atom is shown:

options.text: as a point at the centre of a circle
at the upper end of the line
at the lower end of the line
as a circle behind the rear carbon

solution.concept: Sawhorse projection
solution.explanation: In a sawhorse projection the molecule is viewed along the C–C axis from an oblique angle. The front carbon is at the lower end of the inclined line and the rear carbon at the upper end, each with its three bonds drawn.
steps: Sawhorse: front carbon at the lower end, rear carbon at the upper end
solution.why_others_wrong: A point at the centre of a circle is the front carbon in a Newman projection; the upper end of the line is the rear carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ethene polymerises at high temperature and pressure, in the presence of a catalyst, to give polythene, –(CH₂–CH₂)ₙ–. A polythene chain is made of an average of 2000 ethene units. Ignoring the end groups, its average molar mass is (C = 12, H = 1):

solution.concept: Polymerisation of alkenes

questions.question_text: Linear polymerisation of ethyne gives a high-molecular-mass polyene that conducts electricity under special conditions; thin films of it can be used as electrodes in batteries. The polymer is:

solution.concept: Polymerisation of alkynes
solution.explanation: NCERT describes two kinds of polymerisation of ethyne: linear polymerisation gives polyacetylene (polyethyne), a polyene with alternating double bonds that can conduct electricity, while cyclic polymerisation (red-hot iron tube, 873 K) gives benzene.
solution.why_others_wrong: Polythene and polypropene are made from ethene and propene; benzene is the cyclic trimer of ethyne, not a polymer.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: polymerisation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.0 g of propyne, CH₃–C≡CH, reacts completely with sodium metal to form sodium propynide and hydrogen. The volume of hydrogen evolved at STP is (C = 12, H = 1; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Acidic character of terminal alkynes
solution.explanation: Only the hydrogen attached to the triple-bonded carbon is acidic. Two molecules of propyne react with two sodium atoms to release one molecule of H₂: 2CH₃C≡CH + 2Na → 2CH₃C≡CNa + H₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ethyne is passed into an excess of bromine dissolved in CCl₄ until no more bromine is decolourised. The final product is:

solution.concept: Addition of halogens to alkynes
solution.explanation: Bromine adds in two steps across the triple bond: first to 1,2-dibromoethene and then, with excess bromine, to 1,1,2,2-tetrabromoethane. The reddish-orange colour of bromine is discharged, which is a test for unsaturation.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1,2-Dibromoethane comes from ethene + Br₂; bromoethyne is a substitution product; 1,1-dibromoethane comes from adding two HBr, not Br₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the arenium ion (σ-complex) formed during electrophilic substitution of benzene, one of the ring carbon atoms is sp³ hybridised.
Reason (R): The electrophile forms a σ bond with one ring carbon, which then carries four σ bonds (to H, to the electrophile and to two ring carbons).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Structure of the arenium ion
solution.explanation: When the electrophile attacks, one carbon of the ring uses its π electrons to form a σ bond to E. That carbon now has four σ bonds and no p orbital in the π system, so it is sp³ hybridised; the positive charge is delocalised over the other five carbons. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Attack of E⁺ → new C–E σ bond
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', mechanism of electrophilic substitution
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the free-radical halogenation of alkanes are correct?

(a) Fluorination of alkanes is too violent to be controlled.
(b) In the initiation step of the chlorination of methane, a C–H bond undergoes homolysis.
(c) Ethane is formed as a by-product in the chlorination of methane, in the chain termination step.
(d) Bromination of methane proceeds faster than its chlorination.
(e) In a propagation step, a chlorine free radical removes a hydrogen atom from methane to give a methyl free radical and HCl.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Mechanism of free-radical halogenation
solution.explanation: The reactivity of halogens is F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂; fluorination is too violent. Initiation is the homolysis of the weaker Cl–Cl bond by light or heat. In propagation Cl• abstracts H from CH₄ (giving CH₃• and HCl), and CH₃• attacks Cl₂. In termination, radicals combine: two CH₃• radicals give ethane, explaining its presence.
steps: (b) Cl–Cl, not C–H, is broken in initiation → false
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (b) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: halogenation and its mechanism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: cis-But-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene give the same products on ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O).
Statement II: trans-But-2-ene has a higher boiling point than cis-but-2-ene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Geometrical isomers: chemical and physical properties
solution.explanation: Ozonolysis breaks the C=C bond, so the spatial arrangement is lost and both isomers give two molecules of ethanal. The cis isomer is polar (the bond dipoles do not cancel) and boils at a higher temperature (about 277 K) than the non-polar trans isomer (about 274 K).
steps: II: cis is more polar and boils higher → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: geometrical isomerism and ozonolysis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction of propene in List-I with its main product in List-II.

List-I:
A. HBr (no peroxide)
B. HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide
C. Br₂ in CCl₄

II. CH₃–CH(OSO₃H)–CH₃ (propan-2-yl hydrogensulphate)
III. 1-Bromopropane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Electrophilic and free-radical addition to an unsymmetrical alkene
solution.explanation: HBr and cold concentrated H₂SO₄ add by Markovnikov's rule, putting Br or OSO₃H on C-2. With peroxide, HBr adds by a free-radical path (anti-Markovnikov) to give 1-bromopropane. Bromine adds to both carbons of the double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the free-radical monochlorination of propane at a certain temperature, a secondary hydrogen atom is replaced 4.5 times as fast as a primary hydrogen atom. The percentage of 2-chloropropane in the monochlorinated product is:

solution.concept: Relative reactivity of 1° and 2° hydrogen atoms in halogenation
solution.explanation: The amount of each product is proportional to (number of that type of hydrogen) × (reactivity per hydrogen). Propane has six primary and two secondary hydrogen atoms.
solution.why_others_wrong: 25% counts hydrogen atoms only (2 of 8); 40% is the share of 1-chloropropane; 82% (4.5/5.5) ignores the numbers of hydrogen atoms.
