questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 0.10 mol of a mixture of ethene and ethyne needs exactly 0.14 mol of H₂ for complete hydrogenation to ethane over a nickel catalyst. The percentage of ethyne (by moles) in the mixture is:

solution.concept: Hydrogenation stoichiometry of alkenes and alkynes
solution.explanation: One mole of ethene takes up one mole of H₂, and one mole of ethyne takes up two moles of H₂ to give ethane.
solution.why_others_wrong: 60% is the percentage of ethene; 14% and 28% come from using the hydrogen amount directly.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes and alkynes: addition of hydrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A hydrocarbon X, C₅H₈, reacts with sodamide to form a sodium salt. On hydration with dilute H₂SO₄ and Hg²⁺ it gives a methyl ketone, and on complete hydrogenation it gives 2-methylbutane. X is:

solution.concept: Using reactions to identify an alkyne
solution.explanation: Formation of a sodium salt shows a terminal alkyne (≡C–H). Hydrogenation to 2-methylbutane shows a branched carbon skeleton. The only terminal C₅ alkyne with this skeleton is HC≡C–CH(CH₃)₂, which on hydration gives 3-methylbutan-2-one.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pent-1-yne gives n-pentane on hydrogenation. Pent-2-yne has no acidic hydrogen. 2-Methylbuta-1,3-diene gives 2-methylbutane but has no ≡C–H to react with sodamide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: acidic character and addition reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): cis-But-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene change into each other readily at room temperature.
Reason (R): Rotation about a carbon–carbon double bond is restricted because it would require breaking the π bond.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Restricted rotation and geometrical isomerism
solution.explanation: The π bond is formed by sideways overlap of p orbitals; rotating one carbon relative to the other would destroy this overlap. So rotation is restricted, and the cis and trans isomers are separate, stable compounds that do not interconvert at room temperature. A is false; R is true.
steps: A: geometrical isomers are separable and do not interconvert readily → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: geometrical isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Hydration of but-1-yne with dilute H₂SO₄ in the presence of Hg²⁺ gives butan-2-one.
Statement II: Hydration of but-2-yne under the same conditions gives butanal.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Markovnikov hydration of alkynes
solution.explanation: Water adds to the triple bond through an enol, which changes into the carbonyl compound. For but-1-yne, OH goes to C-2 (Markovnikov), giving butan-2-one. In but-2-yne the triple bond is between C-2 and C-3, so the carbonyl group must form on one of these carbons; both directions give butan-2-one, not an aldehyde.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkynes: addition of water
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: To study optical activity, plane polarised light is used. Ordinary light is converted into plane polarised light by passing it through a:

solution.concept: Plane polarised light and optical activity
solution.explanation: When ordinary light is passed through a Nicol prism (made of calcite), the emerging light vibrates in a single plane. Optically active compounds rotate the plane of this light; the rotation is measured with a polarimeter.
solution.why_others_wrong: A glass prism disperses light into colours; a grating diffracts it; a lens focuses it. None polarises light.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', optical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: DDT, p,p′-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, has the molecular formula C₁₄H₉Cl₅. The percentage of chlorine by mass in DDT is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Percentage composition of a polyhalogen compound
solution.explanation: Molar mass of C₁₄H₉Cl₅ = 14(12) + 9(1) + 5(35.5) = 354.5 g mol⁻¹; five chlorine atoms contribute 177.5 g.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30.0% counts only the three Cl of the CCl₃ group; 40.1% counts four Cl; 10.0% counts one Cl.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds (DDT)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The effectiveness of DDT as an insecticide was discovered by Paul Müller, who received the Nobel Prize in Medicine and Physiology in 1948 for this discovery.
Statement II: Many species of insects have developed resistance to DDT.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: DDT: discovery and problems
solution.explanation: NCERT records that DDT, first prepared in 1873, was found to be an effective insecticide by Paul Müller in 1939, and he received the 1948 Nobel Prize. Its use later caused problems: many insect species became resistant to it, and it is not metabolised rapidly by animals, so it accumulates in fatty tissues.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds (DDT)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A monochloroalkane, CₙH₂ₙ₊₁Cl, contains 38.4% chlorine by mass. Its molecular formula is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.concept: Finding the formula of a haloalkane from its composition
solution.explanation: The compound has one chlorine atom, so its molar mass M = 35.5/0.384 ≈ 92.5 g mol⁻¹. For CₙH₂ₙ₊₁Cl, M = 14n + 36.5.
solution.why_others_wrong: C₃H₇Cl has 45.2% Cl, C₅H₁₁Cl 33.3% and C₂H₅Cl 55.0%.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', classification and nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Freon-12, CCl₂F₂, one of the most common freons in industrial use, is manufactured from tetrachloromethane by the:

solution.concept: Preparation of freons by halogen exchange
solution.explanation: Replacing chlorine by fluorine using a metallic fluoride (such as SbF₃ or AgF) is the Swarts reaction. NCERT states that Freon-12 is made from CCl₄ in this way.
solution.why_others_wrong: The Finkelstein reaction exchanges Cl/Br for I with NaI in acetone; the Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium; the Sandmeyer reaction uses diazonium salts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds (freons)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Chloroform, shaken with aqueous silver nitrate solution, gives an immediate white precipitate of AgCl.
Reason (R): In chloroform the chlorine atoms are covalently bonded to carbon, so free chloride ions are not present.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Covalent halogen and the silver nitrate test
solution.explanation: Silver nitrate precipitates only halide ions. In CHCl₃ the chlorine is held by covalent C–Cl bonds, so no precipitate forms directly; that is why an organic compound is first fused with sodium (Lassaigne's test) to convert covalent halogen into NaX before the AgNO₃ test. A is false, R is true.
steps: A: no free Cl⁻ → no immediate AgCl → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques', detection of halogens
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about elimination and substitution in alkyl halides are correct?

(a) A bulkier nucleophile prefers to act as a base and abstract a proton rather than approach a carbon atom.
(b) A primary alkyl halide prefers to react by the SN2 mechanism.
(c) A tertiary alkyl halide treated with a strong base undergoes the SN2 reaction rather than elimination.
(d) Dehydrohalogenation is called β-elimination because the hydrogen atom is removed from the β-carbon.
(e) A secondary alkyl halide can undergo substitution but never elimination.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Elimination versus substitution
solution.explanation: A species with a lone pair can act as a nucleophile or a base. Bulky reagents find it easier to remove a β-hydrogen than to reach the carbon, so they favour elimination. Primary halides prefer SN2; secondary halides may give SN2 or elimination depending on the base/nucleophile; tertiary halides give SN1 or elimination (steric hindrance blocks SN2).
steps: (c) tertiary halides do not undergo SN2 → false
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (c) or (e), both false, or leave out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', elimination reactions (elimination versus substitution)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the structure in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. CH₃–CHCl–CHBr–CH₃
B. CH₂=CH–CHCl–CH₃
C. (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂Br
D. ClCH₂–C≡C–CH₂Cl

List-II:
I. 1-Bromo-2-methylpropane
II. 2-Bromo-3-chlorobutane
III. 1,4-Dichlorobut-2-yne
IV. 3-Chlorobut-1-ene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: IUPAC names of halogen compounds
solution.explanation: A: both directions give the locants {2, 3}; the tie is broken alphabetically, so bromo gets the lower locant: 2-bromo-3-chlorobutane. B: the double bond gets locant 1 and Cl is on C-3: 3-chlorobut-1-ene. C: the longest chain has three carbons: 1-bromo-2-methylpropane. D: the triple bond is at C-2 and the two Cl atoms at C-1 and C-4: 1,4-dichlorobut-2-yne.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the alkene and the dihalide, or the alkyne and the branched bromide.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The dipole moments of the methyl halides do not simply follow the electronegativity of the halogen. Which of the following has the largest dipole moment?

solution.concept: Dipole moment of the C–X bond: charge and bond length
solution.explanation: Dipole moment depends on both the charge separation and the bond length. C–F is the most polar bond, but it is much shorter than C–Cl; the longer C–Cl bond with a large charge separation gives CH₃Cl the largest dipole moment (NCERT: CH₃F 1.847 D, CH₃Cl 1.860 D, CH₃Br 1.830 D, CH₃I 1.636 D).
steps: C–F: largest charge but shortest bond
solution.why_others_wrong: CH₃F is the common trap (most electronegative halogen); CH₃Br and CH₃I have smaller charge separation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nature of the C–X bond (table of dipole moments)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Propan-1-ol is heated with thionyl chloride to give X. X is heated with silver cyanide to give Y as the main product. Y is:

solution.concept: Alkyl halide from an alcohol, then reaction with an ambident nucleophile
solution.explanation: SOCl₂ replaces –OH by –Cl without changing the carbon skeleton, so X is 1-chloropropane. AgCN is mainly covalent; only the nitrogen lone pair is free to attack, so the main product is an isocyanide: 1-propyl isocyanide, CH₃CH₂CH₂NC.
solution.why_others_wrong: Nitriles (–CN) are the main products with KCN, not AgCN; the isopropyl products would need a change in the carbon chain, which does not occur.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation from alcohols and nucleophilic substitution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In aprotic solvents such as benzene, ethanoic acid molecules associate as hydrogen-bonded dimers. If ethanoic acid were completely dimerised in benzene, the molar mass found from a colligative property would be (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Dimerisation of carboxylic acids
solution.explanation: Two molecules of CH₃COOH (60 g mol⁻¹) are held together by two hydrogen bonds. Complete dimerisation halves the number of particles, so the apparent molar mass doubles.
solution.why_others_wrong: 60 g mol⁻¹ assumes no association; 30 g mol⁻¹ assumes dissociation into two particles; 118 g mol⁻¹ wrongly subtracts two hydrogen atoms for the hydrogen bonds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', physical properties of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Propanone reacts with ethane-1,2-diol (ethylene glycol) in the presence of dry HCl to form a cyclic ketal, 2,2-dimethyl-1,3-dioxolane (C₅H₁₀O₂), and water. The mass of the ketal obtained from 5.8 g of propanone, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Ketal formation from ketones and ethylene glycol
solution.explanation: One mole of ketone reacts with one mole of the diol and loses one mole of water to give one mole of the cyclic ketal.
solution.why_others_wrong: 12.0 g adds the diol but forgets the water lost; 5.8 g is the mass of propanone; 8.4 g has no basis in the equation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', nucleophilic addition of alcohols (ethylene glycol ketals)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following reagents reduces ethanal to ethanol but does NOT reduce ethanoic acid?

solution.concept: Selectivity of reducing agents
solution.explanation: NaBH₄ reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols but does not reduce the carboxyl group. LiAlH₄ and diborane reduce both. Zn–Hg/HCl (Clemmensen) reduces a carbonyl group to CH₂, giving ethane, not ethanol.
solution.why_others_wrong: LiAlH₄ and diborane also reduce carboxylic acids to primary alcohols; Clemmensen reduction gives an alkane.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reduction of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the preparation of ethanol by fermentation, the sugar in molasses is first converted into glucose and fructose by an enzyme. This enzyme is:

solution.concept: Fermentation of sugar to ethanol
solution.explanation: Invertase converts sucrose (from molasses, sugarcane or grapes) into glucose and fructose. Zymase, found in yeast, then ferments these to ethanol and carbon dioxide.
solution.why_others_wrong: Zymase acts in the second step; diastase and maltase act on starch and maltose, not on the sugar of molasses as described.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', commercially important alcohols (ethanol)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Fehling's solution B is an alkaline solution of sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle salt).
Statement II: Tollens' reagent is an alkaline solution of copper(II) sulphate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Composition of Fehling's and Tollens' reagents
solution.explanation: Fehling's reagent is made just before use from Fehling A (aqueous copper sulphate) and Fehling B (alkaline sodium potassium tartrate). Tollens' reagent is freshly prepared ammoniacal silver nitrate solution.
steps: II: Tollens' reagent = ammoniacal AgNO₃ → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', oxidation (Tollens' and Fehling's tests)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the common name in List-I with the IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. Acetophenone
B. Benzophenone
C. Isobutyraldehyde
D. Methyl n-propyl ketone

List-II:
I. 2-Methylpropanal
II. Pentan-2-one
III. Diphenylmethanone
IV. 1-Phenylethan-1-one

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Common and IUPAC names of carbonyl compounds
solution.explanation: Acetophenone is C₆H₅COCH₃ (1-phenylethan-1-one); benzophenone is C₆H₅COC₆H₅ (diphenylmethanone); isobutyraldehyde is (CH₃)₂CHCHO (2-methylpropanal); methyl n-propyl ketone is CH₃COCH₂CH₂CH₃ (pentan-2-one).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the two aromatic ketones or the aldehyde and the aliphatic ketone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The pKa of chloroethanoic acid is 2.86 and that of ethanoic acid is 4.76. The ratio Ka(ClCH₂COOH) / Ka(CH₃COOH) is about (antilog 0.90 = 7.94):

solution.concept: Comparing acid strengths from pKa values
solution.explanation: pKa = −log Ka, so the ratio of Ka values is 10 raised to the difference in pKa. The electron-withdrawing chlorine (−I effect) stabilises the carboxylate ion and raises Ka.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.9 is the difference in pKa, not the ratio of Ka; 7.9 drops a factor of 10; 1.7 is the ratio of the two pKa values (4.76/2.86).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', acidity of carboxylic acids (effect of substituents)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the industrial preparation of phenol, cumene (isopropylbenzene, C₉H₁₂) is oxidised in air to cumene hydroperoxide, which is decomposed by dilute acid. The mass of the by-product propanone obtained from 12.0 g of cumene, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Cumene process: stoichiometry
solution.explanation: One mole of cumene gives one mole of phenol and one mole of propanone.
solution.why_others_wrong: 9.4 g is the mass of phenol; 11.6 g takes two moles of propanone per mole of cumene; 6.0 g uses 60 g mol⁻¹ for propanone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of phenols (from cumene)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Anisole (methoxybenzene) is treated with ethanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃. The main product(s) is/are:

solution.concept: Friedel–Crafts acylation of an aromatic ether
solution.explanation: The –OCH₃ group activates the ring and directs incoming electrophiles to the ortho and para positions (+R effect). In the Friedel–Crafts acylation the electrophile CH₃CO⁺ substitutes the ring, giving 2- and 4-methoxyacetophenone; the ether linkage is not broken.
solution.why_others_wrong: The meta product is not the main one; AlCl₃/CH₃COCl does not cleave the C–O bonds of the ether, so phenyl ethanoate or methanol are not formed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', electrophilic substitution in aromatic ethers
solution.final_answer: Option B: A mixture of 2-methoxyacetophenone and 4-methoxyacetophenone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Toluene is treated with chromic oxide (CrO₃) in acetic anhydride, and the product is hydrolysed with aqueous acid to give benzaldehyde. The intermediate that is hydrolysed is:

solution.concept: Preparation of benzaldehyde from toluene with CrO₃
solution.explanation: In acetic anhydride the methyl group of toluene is oxidised and trapped as benzylidene diacetate, C₆H₅CH(OCOCH₃)₂, which protects the aldehyde from further oxidation. Acid hydrolysis then releases benzaldehyde.
solution.why_others_wrong: Benzoic acid would be over-oxidation; benzyl alcohol and benzoyl chloride are not formed in this reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of aromatic aldehydes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The α-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones are acidic.
Reason (R): The carbonyl group withdraws electrons strongly, and the conjugate base (carbanion) formed by losing an α-hydrogen is stabilised by resonance.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Acidity of α-hydrogens
solution.explanation: NCERT attributes the acidity of α-hydrogens to the strong electron-withdrawing effect of the carbonyl group and to resonance stabilisation of the conjugate base (the negative charge is shared with the oxygen). This acidity is the basis of aldol condensation and the haloform reaction. R explains A.
steps: –I of C=O weakens the α C–H bond
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reactions due to α-hydrogen
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Commercially, carboxylic acids are reduced to alcohols by first converting them into esters and then hydrogenating the esters in the presence of a catalyst.
Statement II: Diborane reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Reduction of carboxylic acids to alcohols
solution.explanation: LiAlH₄ is expensive, so industrially the acid is converted to an ester and the ester is hydrogenated catalytically. Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by LiAlH₄ or, better, by diborane, which does not easily reduce ester, nitro or halo groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of alcohols; 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reduction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the common name of the ether in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. Anisole
B. Phenetole
C. Methyl isopropyl ether
D. Diethyl ether

List-II:
I. Ethoxyethane
II. 2-Methoxypropane
III. Methoxybenzene
IV. Ethoxybenzene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Nomenclature of ethers
solution.explanation: In IUPAC names, ethers are named as alkoxy derivatives of the larger hydrocarbon. Anisole is C₆H₅OCH₃ (methoxybenzene), phenetole is C₆H₅OC₂H₅ (ethoxybenzene), methyl isopropyl ether is CH₃OCH(CH₃)₂ (2-methoxypropane), and diethyl ether is ethoxyethane.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap anisole and phenetole or the two aliphatic ethers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', nomenclature of ethers
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the acid-catalysed esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol, the carbonyl oxygen is first protonated and the alcohol then adds to the carbonyl carbon. The molecule of water eliminated takes its oxygen atom from:

options.text: the sulphuric acid used as catalyst
the alcohol and the acid in equal proportion

solution.concept: Mechanism of esterification (nucleophilic acyl substitution)
solution.explanation: After the alcohol adds, a proton transfer in the tetrahedral intermediate converts one of the acid's oxygen groups into –OH₂⁺, a good leaving group, which leaves as water. The alcohol oxygen stays in the ester as the –OR group.
steps: Alcohol oxygen attacks carbonyl carbon (stays in ester)
–OH₂⁺ formed from an acid oxygen leaves as H₂O
solution.why_others_wrong: The alcohol oxygen becomes the ester's –O–R; H₂SO₄ is only a catalyst and is regenerated.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', esterification (mechanism)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 9.4 g of phenol is converted into salicylic acid by Kolbe's reaction, and the salicylic acid is then acetylated to aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid, C₉H₈O₄). If the overall yield is 80%, the mass of aspirin obtained is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Two-step synthesis with an overall yield
solution.explanation: Sodium phenoxide reacts with CO₂ (Kolbe's reaction) to give, after acidification, salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). Acetylation of its –OH group gives aspirin. One mole of phenol gives one mole of aspirin at 100% yield.
solution.why_others_wrong: 18.0 g ignores the yield; 13.8 g is the theoretical mass of salicylic acid; 11.0 g is 80% of the salicylic acid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', Kolbe's reaction and acetylation of salicylic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the esterification CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O, Kc = 4 at the temperature of the experiment. If 1.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 1.0 mol of ethanol are allowed to reach equilibrium, the amount of ester formed is:

solution.concept: Reversibility of esterification
solution.explanation: Esterification is reversible. With x mol of ester and x mol of water formed, (1 − x) mol of each reactant remains; the volume cancels because Δn = 0.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.80 mol solves x/(1 − x) = 4 (no square root); 0.50 mol assumes Kc = 1; 0.33 mol is the amount of acid left.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', esterification; Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium'

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The pKa of phenol is 10.0. Treating phenol as a weak monobasic acid, the pH of a 0.010 M aqueous solution of phenol is:

solution.concept: Weak acidity of phenol
solution.explanation: For a weak acid with small ionisation, [H⁺] = √(Ka·C).
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.0 and 4.0 come from wrong square roots; 12.0 adds pKa and −log C without halving.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of phenols; Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium'

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following comparisons of acid strength are correct?

(a) 4-Nitrobenzoic acid is a stronger acid than benzoic acid.
(b) 4-Methoxybenzoic acid is a stronger acid than benzoic acid.
(c) CF₃COOH is a stronger acid than CCl₃COOH.
(d) Phenylethanoic acid (C₆H₅CH₂COOH) is a stronger acid than benzoic acid.
(e) Ethanoic acid is a stronger acid than propanoic acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Effect of substituents on the acidity of carboxylic acids
solution.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups (–NO₂, –CF₃, –CCl₃) stabilise the carboxylate ion and increase acidity; fluorine withdraws more strongly than chlorine. Electron-donating groups (–OCH₃, alkyl) decrease it. A phenyl group attached directly to –COOH increases acidity, but the effect falls when a CH₂ group separates them. NCERT's order includes CF₃COOH > CCl₃COOH and C₆H₅COOH > C₆H₅CH₂COOH > CH₃COOH > CH₃CH₂COOH.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (b) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', effect of substituents on acidity

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Benzene is treated with ethanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous AlCl₃ to give X. X is warmed with iodine and aqueous NaOH to give a yellow precipitate and a salt Y. Acidification of Y gives Z. Z is:

solution.concept: Friedel–Crafts acylation followed by the haloform reaction
solution.explanation: Friedel–Crafts acylation gives acetophenone, C₆H₅COCH₃ (X). As a methyl ketone it gives the iodoform reaction: the CH₃ group becomes CHI₃ (yellow precipitate) and the rest becomes sodium benzoate (Y). Acidification gives benzoic acid (Z).
solution.why_others_wrong: The haloform reaction removes one carbon (the methyl), so the acid has the same carbon count as the benzoyl group, not phenylethanoic acid. No aldehyde or phenol is formed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of ketones and the haloform reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): p-Nitrophenol is a stronger acid than m-nitrophenol.
Reason (R): At the para position the –NO₂ group withdraws electrons by both the −I and −R effects and delocalises the negative charge of the phenoxide ion onto itself, whereas at the meta position only its −I effect operates.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Position of a substituent and the acidity of phenols
solution.explanation: NCERT gives pKa values of 7.1 for p-nitrophenol and 8.3 for m-nitrophenol. At the para position the negative charge of the phenoxide ion can be delocalised onto the nitro group by resonance; at the meta position it cannot, so only the weaker inductive effect helps. R explains A.
steps: Lower pKa for p-nitrophenol; R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of phenols (Table of pKa values)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Methanamine is treated repeatedly with iodomethane until the quaternary ammonium salt, (CH₃)₄N⁺I⁻, is formed. The minimum number of moles of CH₃I consumed per mole of methanamine is:

solution.concept: Alkylation of amines
solution.explanation: Each reaction with CH₃I replaces one N–H hydrogen by a methyl group (and finally adds a fourth methyl to form the quaternary salt). Methanamine already carries one methyl group, so three more are needed.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 and 2 stop at the secondary or tertiary amine; 4 counts the methyl group already present.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', chemical reactions: alkylation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In Hinsberg's test for distinguishing primary, secondary and tertiary amines, benzenesulphonyl chloride is nowadays replaced by:

solution.concept: Hinsberg's reagent
solution.explanation: NCERT notes that benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent) has now been replaced by p-toluenesulphonyl chloride, which reacts with primary and secondary amines in the same way to give sulphonamides.
steps: Hinsberg's test: ArSO₂Cl with 1°, 2° and 3° amines
solution.why_others_wrong: Benzoyl and ethanoyl chlorides give amides (acylation), not sulphonamides; chloroform with ethanolic KOH is the carbylamine test.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', reaction with arylsulphonyl chloride

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The order of reactivity of alkyl halides with ammonia or amines is RI > RBr > RCl.
Statement II: The free amine is obtained from the ammonium salt formed in ammonolysis by treating the salt with a strong acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Ammonolysis of alkyl halides
solution.explanation: NCERT gives the reactivity order RI > RBr > RCl. Ammonolysis first gives the substituted ammonium salt; the free amine is released by treating this salt with a strong base (which removes H⁺), not with an acid.
steps: II: a strong base is needed → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', preparation by ammonolysis of alkyl halides
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Aniline is heated with concentrated H₂SO₄; the anilinium hydrogensulphate first formed is heated at 453–473 K to give sulphanilic acid (4-aminobenzenesulphonic acid, C₆H₇NO₃S). The mass of sulphanilic acid obtained from 9.3 g of aniline, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32):

solution.concept: Sulphonation of aniline
solution.explanation: One mole of aniline gives one mole of sulphanilic acid. The intermediate salt, anilinium hydrogensulphate, loses water on heating.
solution.why_others_wrong: 19.1 g is the mass of anilinium hydrogensulphate (water not lost); 8.7 g halves the answer; 15.5 g has no basis in the equation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', electrophilic substitution: sulphonation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂–N(CH₃)–CH₂CH₃ is:

solution.concept: Naming tertiary amines
solution.explanation: In a secondary or tertiary amine, the longest alkyl group on nitrogen gives the parent name (propan-1-amine here); the other groups are cited with the locant N and listed alphabetically: N-ethyl, N-methyl.
steps: Largest group on N: propyl → propan-1-amine
solution.why_others_wrong: Ethanamine and methanamine are not built on the largest alkyl group; 3-methylhexan-3-amine is a primary amine with a different structure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the structure and classification of amines are correct?

(a) The nitrogen atom in amines is sp³ hybridised and the geometry around it is pyramidal.
(b) Benzylamine, C₆H₅CH₂NH₂, is an arylamine.
(c) The C–N–C bond angle in trimethylamine is about 108°.
(d) Amines may be regarded as derivatives of ammonia in which hydrogen atoms are replaced by alkyl or aryl groups.
(e) N,N-Dimethylaniline is a secondary amine.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structure and classification of amines
solution.explanation: Nitrogen uses three sp³ orbitals for bonds; the fourth holds the lone pair, so amines are pyramidal and the C–N–C angle in trimethylamine is 108°, a little less than 109.5°. In an arylamine the –NH₂ group is bonded directly to the ring; benzylamine has it on a CH₂ group, so it is not an arylamine. N,N-dimethylaniline has no H on nitrogen: it is a tertiary amine.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (b) or (e), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', structure and classification

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with the amine formed in List-II.

List-I:
A. CH₃CN, reduced with LiAlH₄
B. CH₃CONH₂ + Br₂ + NaOH
C. C₆H₅CH₂Cl + large excess of NH₃
D. C₆H₅CONH₂ + Br₂ + NaOH

List-II:
I. Aniline
II. Ethanamine
III. Benzylamine
IV. Methanamine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Methods of preparing amines
solution.explanation: Reducing a nitrile adds two H₂ to C≡N with no loss of carbon: CH₃CN → CH₃CH₂NH₂. Hofmann bromamide degradation gives an amine with one carbon fewer: CH₃CONH₂ → CH₃NH₂ and C₆H₅CONH₂ → C₆H₅NH₂. Ammonolysis with excess ammonia gives mainly the primary amine: benzylamine.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes forget that Hofmann degradation removes one carbon, or that nitrile reduction keeps all the carbons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', preparation of amines
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The pKb of methanamine is 3.38 and that of aniline is 9.38. For 0.01 M aqueous solutions of the two amines, each only slightly ionised, the ratio [OH⁻](methanamine) / [OH⁻](aniline) is about:

solution.concept: Basic strength from pKb and the hydroxide ion concentration
solution.explanation: For a weak base, [OH⁻] = √(Kb·C). At equal concentrations, the ratio of [OH⁻] is the square root of the ratio of the Kb values.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10⁶ is the ratio of Kb values (square root not taken); 6 and 3 confuse the pKb difference with the ratio.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', basic character (pKb values); Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium'

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Aniline is acetylated to X. X is nitrated with a mixture of concentrated HNO₃ and H₂SO₄ to give Y as the main product, and Y is hydrolysed to Z. Z is diazotised at 273–278 K and the diazonium salt is treated with hypophosphorous acid (H₃PO₂) and water. The final product is:

solution.concept: Using the amino group as a temporary directing group
solution.explanation: Acetylation gives acetanilide (X); nitration gives mainly 4-nitroacetanilide (Y); hydrolysis gives 4-nitroaniline (Z). Diazotisation and reduction with H₃PO₂ replace the –N₂⁺ group by hydrogen, leaving nitrobenzene.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4-Nitrophenol would need warming of the diazonium salt with water; aniline and 4-nitroacetanilide are earlier compounds in the sequence.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', nitration of aniline and reactions of diazonium salts

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Fluorobenzene and iodobenzene are conveniently prepared from benzenediazonium salts rather than from benzene.
Reason (R): Aryl fluorides and aryl iodides cannot be prepared conveniently by direct halogenation of benzene.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Importance of diazonium salts in synthesis
solution.explanation: Direct fluorination of benzene is too violent and direct iodination is reversible, so these haloarenes are made from diazonium salts: with KI for iodobenzene, and via the fluoroborate (HBF₄, then heat) for fluorobenzene. NCERT gives this as a reason for the importance of diazonium salts. R explains A.
steps: Direct F₂: too violent; direct I₂: reversible
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Amines', importance of diazonium salts in synthesis of aromatic compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The letters D and L before the names of sugars such as D-glucose indicate the relative configuration of the molecule. The reference compound for assigning D or L is:

solution.concept: D/L configuration of sugars
solution.explanation: The configuration is compared with that of glyceraldehyde: (+)-glyceraldehyde has the D configuration. A sugar is D if the –OH on its lowest asymmetric carbon is on the right (as in D-glyceraldehyde). D and L do not tell the direction of optical rotation.
steps: –OH on the right at the lowest asymmetric carbon → D
solution.why_others_wrong: Glucose and fructose are the sugars being named, not the reference; glycine has no asymmetric carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', configuration of monosaccharides (D/L)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the hormone in List-I with its chemical nature in List-II.

List-I:
A. Insulin
B. Testosterone
C. Epinephrine (adrenaline)
D. Thyroxine

List-II:
I. Iodothyronine
II. Steroid
III. Polypeptide (protein)
IV. Amino acid derivative

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Chemical nature of hormones
solution.explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers of different kinds: insulin is a polypeptide (protein) hormone, testosterone a steroid, epinephrine an amino acid derivative, and thyroxine an iodothyronine (an iodinated derivative of tyrosine).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes interchange the steroid and polypeptide hormones or the two tyrosine-derived hormones.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', mechanism of hormone action (classes of hormones)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Cellulose is a straight-chain polysaccharide made only of β-D-glucose units. It is the predominant constituent of:

options.text: The liver and muscles of animals
The cell wall of plant cells

solution.concept: Occurrence of cellulose
solution.explanation: Cellulose occurs exclusively in plants and is the most abundant organic substance in the plant kingdom; it is the main constituent of plant cell walls. Glycogen (not cellulose) is stored in animal liver and muscle.
steps: Glycogen → animal liver, muscle and brain
solution.why_others_wrong: Liver and muscle store glycogen; cane sugar is sucrose; milk sugar is lactose.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides (cellulose)
solution.final_answer: Option D: The cell wall of plant cells

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A double-stranded DNA segment has 100 base pairs, of which 30 are A–T pairs and the rest are G–C pairs. An A–T pair is held by two hydrogen bonds and a G–C pair by three. The total number of hydrogen bonds between the two strands of this segment is:

solution.concept: Complementary base pairing in DNA
solution.explanation: Adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine. The number of G–C pairs is 100 − 30 = 70.
solution.why_others_wrong: 230 swaps the hydrogen-bond numbers of the two pairs; 200 gives every pair two bonds; 250 averages them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', structure of polynucleotide chain; Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Amylose is a linear polymer of α-D-glucose, represented as (C₆H₁₀O₅)ₙ. A sample of amylose has a molar mass of 81000 g mol⁻¹. Ignoring the end groups, the number of glucose units in each chain is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.concept: Repeating unit of polysaccharides
solution.explanation: Each glucose unit in the chain has lost one molecule of water in forming the glycosidic links, so the repeating unit is C₆H₁₀O₅ (162 g mol⁻¹), not C₆H₁₂O₆ (180 g mol⁻¹).
solution.why_others_wrong: 450 divides by 180 (glucose itself); 1000 and 250 are off by a factor of two.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', polysaccharides (starch: amylose)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A sucrose solution that has been boiled with dilute acid gives a red precipitate with Fehling's solution, although sucrose itself does not.
Reason (R): Acid hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose, both of which are reducing sugars.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Hydrolysis of a non-reducing sugar
solution.explanation: In sucrose the reducing groups of glucose (C1) and fructose (C2) are tied up in the glycosidic bond, so it does not reduce Fehling's solution. Hydrolysis frees these groups: glucose and fructose are both reducing sugars and give red Cu₂O. R explains A.
steps: Both reduce Fehling's solution → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', disaccharides (sucrose)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about nucleic acids are correct?

(a) DNA is responsible for maintaining the identity of different species of organisms over millions of years.
(b) Proteins are synthesised by RNA molecules in the cell, but the message for the synthesis of a particular protein is present in DNA.
(c) In RNA, thymine takes the place of uracil.
(d) Nucleotides are joined to one another by peptide bonds.
(e) Nucleic acids are long-chain polymers of nucleotides, so they are also called polynucleotides.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structure and biological functions of nucleic acids
solution.explanation: DNA is the chemical basis of heredity and carries the message for protein synthesis, which is carried out by the different RNAs. RNA contains uracil in place of thymine (not the reverse). Nucleotides are linked by phosphodiester bonds; peptide bonds join amino acids. Nucleic acids are polynucleotides.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (c) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', nucleic acids (biological functions)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the evidence for the structure of glucose are correct?

(a) Prolonged heating with HI gives n-hexane, showing that the six carbon atoms are linked in a straight chain.
(b) Oxidation with bromine water to gluconic acid shows that the carbonyl group of glucose is a ketone group.
(c) Glucose and gluconic acid are both oxidised by nitric acid to saccharic acid, which shows that glucose contains a primary alcohol (–CH₂OH) group.
(d) Formation of a cyanohydrin with HCN shows that glucose contains a primary alcohol group.
(e) The six-membered cyclic form of glucose is called the pyranose structure, by analogy with pyran.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Reactions used to establish the structure of glucose
solution.explanation: HI reduction to n-hexane shows a straight chain. HCN addition and oxime formation show a carbonyl group. Oxidation by a mild agent (bromine water) to a six-carbon acid shows that the carbonyl group is an aldehyde. Oxidation of both glucose and gluconic acid to saccharic acid shows a primary alcohol group. The cyclic six-membered form is called pyranose (like pyran).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (b) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', glucose: structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Maltose is a reducing sugar because, in solution, a free aldehyde group can be produced at C1 of its second glucose unit.
Statement II: Lactose is a non-reducing sugar because the reducing groups of both its monosaccharide units are used in the glycosidic bond.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Reducing and non-reducing disaccharides
solution.explanation: In maltose, C1 of one α-D-glucose is linked to C4 of the other; C1 of the second unit is free and can open to an aldehyde, so maltose is reducing. In lactose, C1 of β-D-galactose is linked to C4 of β-D-glucose; C1 of the glucose unit is free, so lactose is also a reducing sugar. Only sucrose, among these, has both reducing groups tied up.
steps: II: lactose has a free C1 on its glucose unit → reducing → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', disaccharides (maltose and lactose)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Amino acids are colourless, crystalline solids with high melting points and are soluble in water, unlike simple amines and carboxylic acids of similar molecular mass.
Reason (R): In aqueous solution and in the solid, amino acids exist as dipolar ions (zwitterions), which give them a salt-like character.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Zwitterion and the physical properties of amino acids
solution.explanation: The –COOH group loses a proton and the –NH₂ group gains one, giving H₃N⁺–CHR–COO⁻. Strong electrostatic attractions between these dipolar ions make amino acids behave like salts: high melting points and solubility in water. NCERT links the high melting points directly to this dipolar, salt-like character. R explains A.
steps: Zwitterion: –NH₃⁺ and –COO⁻ in the same molecule
Ionic (salt-like) attractions → high m.p., water soluble
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', amino acids (zwitterion)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Potash alum, K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O, is prepared in the laboratory from potassium sulphate and aluminium sulphate. The percentage by mass of water of crystallisation in potash alum is (K = 39, Al = 27, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1):

solution.concept: Composition of a double salt
solution.why_others_wrong: 54.4% is the anhydrous part; 22.8% halves the water; 1.9% counts only one water molecule.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of potash alum

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the analysis of group V cations, the solution is treated with ammonium oxalate solution, and a white precipitate is obtained. This confirms the presence of:

solution.concept: Confirmatory test for calcium ions
solution.explanation: Ca²⁺ ions form a white precipitate of calcium oxalate with ammonium oxalate. Calcium also gives a brick-red flame.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cu²⁺ (group II) and Fe³⁺ (group III) are removed long before group V; NH₄⁺ is tested separately with NaOH and Nessler's reagent.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), systematic analysis of cations (group V)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Detection of elements and functional groups
questions.question_text: An organic compound is heated with phthalic anhydride and a few drops of concentrated H₂SO₄, and the melt is poured into dilute NaOH solution. A pink (red) colour appears. This phthalein dye test shows the presence of:

solution.concept: Phthalein dye test
solution.explanation: Phenols condense with phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ to give phenolphthalein (from phenol), which is pink to red in alkaline solution.
solution.why_others_wrong: Aldehydes are detected with Tollens' or Fehling's reagent, carboxyl groups with NaHCO₃, and primary aromatic amines with the azo dye test.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), tests for functional groups (phenolic group)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the titration of oxalic acid with KMnO₄ the flask is warmed to 50–60 °C, but in the titration of Mohr's salt with KMnO₄ the solution is NOT heated. This is because, on heating, the Mohr's salt solution:

options.text: would lose its ammonium ions as ammonia
would have its Fe²⁺ ions oxidised by atmospheric oxygen
would precipitate iron(III) hydroxide only in the presence of excess acid

solution.concept: Conditions of redox titrations
solution.explanation: The oxalate reaction is slow at room temperature, so it is warmed. Fe²⁺ reacts quickly with MnO₄⁻ at room temperature, and heating would only allow some Fe²⁺ to be oxidised by air to Fe³⁺, giving a low titre.
steps: Mohr's salt: fast reaction; heating → Fe²⁺ oxidised by air → avoid
solution.why_others_wrong: The Fe²⁺–MnO₄⁻ reaction is already fast; ammonium ions do not interfere in acid solution; the last option has no basis.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (Mohr's salt against KMnO₄)
solution.final_answer: Option C: would have its Fe²⁺ ions oxidised by atmospheric oxygen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 200 mL of 0.10 M HCl is mixed with 100 mL of 0.10 M NaOH. Taking the enthalpy of neutralisation of a strong acid by a strong base as −57.1 kJ mol⁻¹, the heat evolved is:

solution.concept: Heat of neutralisation with a limiting reagent
solution.explanation: Heat is released only for the moles of water formed, which equal the moles of the limiting reagent. HCl = 0.020 mol and NaOH = 0.010 mol, so NaOH is limiting.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1142 J uses the moles of HCl; 1713 J adds the moles of acid and base; 285 J halves the correct value.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), thermochemistry: enthalpy of neutralisation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the kinetic study of the reaction Na₂S₂O₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + SO₂ + S + H₂O, 50.0 mL of 0.10 M sodium thiosulphate reacts completely with excess HCl. The mass of sulphur precipitated is (S = 32):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the thiosulphate–acid reaction
solution.explanation: Each thiosulphate ion gives one atom of colloidal sulphur (the other sulphur appears as SO₂).
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.32 g counts both sulphur atoms as precipitated; 0.08 g halves the answer; 0.24 g has no basis in the equation.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), chemical kinetics: reaction of sodium thiosulphate with hydrochloric acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the cation in List-I (with the reagent used) with the observation in List-II.

List-I:
A. Fe³⁺ with potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II)
B. Cu²⁺ with potassium hexacyanidoferrate(II) (acetic acid)
C. Ba²⁺ with potassium chromate
D. Zn²⁺ with sodium hydroxide solution

List-II:
I. Yellow precipitate
II. White precipitate that dissolves in excess of the reagent
III. Prussian blue precipitate
IV. Chocolate-brown precipitate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Confirmatory tests for cations
solution.explanation: Fe³⁺ gives Prussian blue (iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II)) with potassium ferrocyanide; Cu²⁺ gives a chocolate-brown precipitate of Cu₂[Fe(CN)₆]; Ba²⁺ gives yellow BaCrO₄; Zn²⁺ gives white Zn(OH)₂ that dissolves in excess NaOH as zincate.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the two ferrocyanide precipitates or the chromate and hydroxide tests.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), confirmatory tests for cations
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Iron(II) oxalate, FeC₂O₄ (molar mass 144 g mol⁻¹), is titrated with acidified KMnO₄. Both the Fe²⁺ ion and the oxalate ion are oxidised (to Fe³⁺ and CO₂). If a sample needs 30.0 mL of 0.020 M KMnO₄, the mass of FeC₂O₄ in the sample is:

solution.concept: Redox titration when both ions of a salt are oxidised
solution.explanation: MnO₄⁻ gains 5 electrons (Mn +7 → +2). Each FeC₂O₄ loses 3 electrons: one from Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ and two from C₂O₄²⁻ → 2CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.216 g counts only the oxalate (2 e⁻); 0.432 g counts only Fe²⁺ (1 e⁻); 0.0864 g takes 5 e⁻ per FeC₂O₄.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis with KMnO₄ (oxalate and Fe²⁺)

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about titrations with potassium permanganate are correct?

(a) The end point is the first permanent light pink colour of the solution.
(b) Dilute HCl is suitable for acidifying the solution.
(c) Oxalic acid dihydrate can be used as a primary standard.
(d) Phenolphthalein is added as the indicator.
(e) In the titration of oxalic acid, decolourisation is slow at first and becomes rapid as the Mn²⁺ ions formed catalyse the reaction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Practical points in permanganate titrations
solution.explanation: KMnO₄ acts as its own indicator: the first excess drop gives a permanent light pink colour. Dilute H₂SO₄ is used because HCl would itself be oxidised by permanganate (to chlorine), giving a high titre. Oxalic acid dihydrate is a stable, pure crystalline solid and serves as a primary standard. Mn²⁺ ions formed in the reaction catalyse it (autocatalysis).
steps: (b) HCl is oxidised by KMnO₄ → false
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options include (b) or (d), both false.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (redox titrations)

questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The enthalpy of neutralisation of any strong acid by any strong base in dilute solution is nearly the same, about −57 kJ mol⁻¹.
Reason (R): In dilute solution strong acids and strong bases are completely ionised, so the only reaction in every case is H⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq) → H₂O(l).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Constancy of the enthalpy of neutralisation
solution.explanation: Because strong acids, strong bases and their salts are fully ionised, the other ions are spectators. The net change is always the formation of one mole of water from H⁺ and OH⁻, so the enthalpy change is the same. R explains A.
steps: Net: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O in every case
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), thermochemistry: enthalpy of neutralisation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
